title: A Majorana Formulation of Time-Dependent Two-Particle Reduced-Density-Matrix Dynamics
abstract: We introduce a time-dependent two-particle (TP) reduced-density-matrix algorithm for systems of interacting Majorana fermions. We close the BBGKY hierarchy at the two-particle level by reconstructing the three-particle reduced density matrix from lower-order correlations. To stabilize the evolution, we impose a positivity projection on the two-particle density matrix while preserving chosen conserved quantities such as the energy. We benchmark the approach on quenches in the one-dimensional Hubbard model and on flux dynamics in the Kitaev honeycomb model. For the Hubbard quench, TP captures strong-coupling dynamics missed by Hartree--Fock (HF). For the Kitaev quenches, TP accurately reproduces the early-time flux dynamics in several regimes and provides a substantial improvement over HF when two-particle correlations are important. We further show that gauge coherence is essential for flux dynamics. The projection procedure however introduces an effective irreversibility, which affects the long-time dynamics.
summary: This work introduces a time-dependent two-particle reduced-density-matrix algorithm to simulate interacting Majorana fermions. By systematically closing the correlation hierarchy at the two-particle level, the method accurately captures strong-coupling effects in models like the Hubbard and Kitaev systems. While the projection procedure introduces irreversibility, it represents a significant theoretical step beyond mean-field theory for non-equilibrium quantum dynamics.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of simulating time-dependent dynamics in interacting fermionic systems by developing a two-particle reduced-density-matrix (aRDM) approach.
main_result: The two-particle approach successfully captures strong-coupling dynamics in the Hubbard model and accurately reproduces early-time flux dynamics in the Kitaev model, significantly outperforming mean-field approximations.
method: The methodology involves solving the time-dependent BBGKY hierarchy truncated at the two-particle level, utilizing antisymmetrized reduced density matrices (aRDMs) and employing projective purification to enforce physical constraints.
model_or_system: The methods are benchmarked on two key models: quenches in the one-dimensional Hubbard model and flux dynamics in the Kitaev honeycomb model, both involving interacting Majorana fermions.
key_observables: Time evolution of occupation numbers (e.g., $\langle \hat{n}_{1,\uparrow} angle$) and flux weights ($	ext{W}_A$).
important_parameters: Interaction strength ($U/J_h$) and magnetic field strength ($h/J$).
main_assumptions: The primary approximations are truncating the correlation hierarchy at the two-particle level and using a projective purification step to maintain positivity, which introduces effective irreversibility.
figures_summary: Figure 2 compares the time evolution of occupation numbers for the Hubbard model at weak and strong coupling, showing TP tracking exact results better than HF. Other figures compare flux dynamics across various approximations (TP, HF, etc.) in the Kitaev model.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the TP algorithm for Majorana fermions, details the aRDM truncation and stabilization via projection, and then benchmarks this method on two distinct physical systems: the Hubbard quench and the Kitaev flux dynamics.
why_interesting: The development of a controlled, systematic method to go beyond mean-field theory for strongly correlated systems, while managing the complexity of higher-order correlations, is highly relevant for understanding non-equilibrium quantum dynamics in condensed matter.
